I mean, who cares about universities and lawyers and things like that when all you wanna know is how to order a beer, a coffee, or some food? It’s definitely designed much more for people moving to a country or something like that, not a great app if you just wanna curious about the language and wanna learn some basic talents in which they would add something like that and have the ability to not learn written language because it’s just way more difficult to learn written language in three months, it’s not possible.

reviews.title: Worse and worse and worse
reviews.text: They must have finally realized that people didn’t want to pay for a premium-tier account that only gets you more AI slop. I used to pay for premium in the old days because I wanted this app to stay in business but I stopped when they did their the “AI-first” layoffs. Now they charge you real money to buy streak freezes. I’ve used this app for years, they used to have free discussion forums for each exercise, they used to teach you grammar rules instead of just random sentences, they used to let you earn streak freezes by doing exercises, it used to be made by real actual people instead of AI. 2000+ day streak but it’s time to jump ship.

reviews.title: Duolingo
reviews.text: Overall this app is a very helpful app and it is really useful for learning languages, chess, or math. I’ve used Duolingo for mostly chess but also Spanish and Russian. The reason I’m giving Duolingo a 3/5 is because of the horrible energy situation. I’m speaking on behalf of the chess learning but when you learn a lesson, you lose around 10 energy. When you review a match, lose 10 energy. And you only get 25 energy with an additional 5 energy per hour. So unless you watch a million adds or get the Duolingo plan you’re stuck at only a couple lessons a day. I also hate the puzzle piece game that they are doing rn. To explain it shortly it’s basically that you get a puzzle piece for completing 1, 2, 4, and 6 lessons. Once you complete the puzzle you get a skin and there are about 6 skins. It sounds great in theory but they made it to where you get duplicates so even after getting a couple puzzle pieces a day and spending 3000 gems I only have 4 skins. I just hope that they stop being so stingy with all of their stuff

reviews.title: The app is not fully compatible with VoiceOver on the iPhone.
reviews.text:
Hello, I am learning English using your app, and I am blind. After several updates, the app has become incompatible with accessibility features, particularly VoiceOver, which is designed for visually impaired and blind users on Apple devices such as the iPhone and iPad.

When I am asked to translate a sentence from Arabic into English or vice versa, VoiceOver no longer moves between the individual words so I can select them and arrange them to form the sentence. As a result, I can no longer use the app.

In previous updates, there were also issues with Arabic sentence ordering. When I selected a word using VoiceOver, it would select the preceding word instead. In the latest update, VoiceOver no longer navigates to the words at all.

This accessibility issue needs to be fixed as soon as possible so that blind users can use the app independently. Please address this problem in a future update.

reviews.title: Learning is no longer the goal
reviews.text:
I've used Duolingo off and on for years, long enough to remember the good old days when learning was actually the focus. 
It really feels like opening one of those gambling apps. Just an overstimulating slot machine of chests, gems, power ups, widgets and constant pressure to upgrade to super. Which, fine, nothing in life is free so I could tolerate a few adds for an accessible learning program. But there's so much other stuff, my time using the app is only 20% actual learning. 
It's so sad, this used to be such a wonderful resource. It really feels worthless now.

reviews.title: Pretty Good but...
reviews.text: I really love this app because it is helping me improve my Spanish speaking skills in a way that I find to be both fun and helpful. However there are a few reasons why I did not give it a full 5 stars. First, there are different ways to speak the Spanish language and simply learning it from Spain limits it. Words are much different than the Spanish I am used to speaking here in America. I am from Puerto Rico. Secondly, if you complete lessons during event challenges you can earn puzzle pieces to unlock suits. Well you have the option to use your gems to buy the pieces you missed, and after spending 1600 gems on 5 pieces, NONE of them were new. They were ALL duplicates! I find that to be extremely unfair and that is a large amount of gems to pay to receive all duplicates. I get that many of these games earn money buy doing this, especially when the app itself is free, but there should be some kind of incentive for spending our gems. Those gems require time spent and learning lessons, to be earned, so make it more fair for those of us who work hard to earn these gems and throw us a bone....and the merchandise is very cute!!!!! But $30 for a small stuffed animal is overkill.

reviews.title: Antithetic Learning: Discrepancy in Lexical State & Discouragement of Progress lost by Energy limit
reviews.text:
First of all,
in “Practice: Review Words” chapter, there are brand new words and sentence structures as questions where the user never learned in any lessons beforehand. 
Antithetical to the eponymous purpose of revising learned vocabulary and lexical structures. 

Besides that,
the energy stopping learners to continue and they will lose all progress is such a deterrent way to turn passionate users away and even quit the app.
With such low limited energy max, the amount of 5 energy the user can obtain at a time, users always end up in 21-24 energy, but they can be all used up even the learner only have one minor hiccup, and then they are forced to buy something to save it (using “inside currency” or “real currency”)
If the learner does not comply, they will lose their progress with all time and energy spent. 

Counterintuitive and very discouraging. 

There are some useful words in this app, if it let you complete the lesson and propel one’s progress.  

Hence, not a fast learning apps.

reviews.title: Main problem
reviews.text: Duolingo is pretty good for making learning new languages  entertaining and in short lessons. However, a big complaint of mine is that they try to get you to purchase the premium package by having your "duo battery" run out pretty quick which sometimes not does not allow you to finish your lesson. Which is very frustrating. You can try to recharge your battery through earning very little points while doing your lesson or watching an advertisement. However, it's still not enough for you to complete a lesson sometimes. Pretty frustrating when you complete most of a lesson only to be told you must quit and t lose that progress. C'mon Duo... you already make money off your ads or people paying premium not to have the ads...
